conversation.text: I spent 200 on matatu and 150 on lunch
Got it! Recorded KES 200 for transport and KES 150 for lunch. Quick tip: Carrying lunch from home a few days a week usually costs less than buying it daily.

summary.summary: In this session, you logged a total expenditure of KES 350 covering your matatu fare and lunch. Tracking these regular daily costs is a great step toward taking full control of your money. With a few small adjustments, you can easily keep more shillings in your pocket.
ways_to_save: Carry a packed lunch from home a few times a week to cut down on daily food costs.
Board matatus slightly before or after peak hours to take advantage of lower off-peak fares.
Set aside any daily change into an M-Pesa Lock Savings account or piggy bank at the end of the day.
